utterances.text: Can you recall what Mr. Dokmanovic actually said in relation to this to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he said that he had been meeting with members of ICTY. He indicated that there were some issues on his mind that he wanted to discuss, in particular he was interested in property rights of the ethnic Serbian people, and specifically about his own property rights relating to the land holdings that he had in Eastern Slavonija, and what would happen to those as that territory reintegrated into the Republic of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After he had told you this, what did you say to him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I had indicated to him that it was my belief that the Transitional Administrator would be willing to meet with him and we then discussed the time and the mechanism of that occurring.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you discuss with him in relation to the time of the meeting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We discussed him meeting with the Transitional Administrator at 3.30 on Friday 27th June in Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why was this time selected?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because that is the time that was available in the Transitional Administrator's calendar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In relation to the travel arrangements, what discussions did you have concerning that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When Mr. Dokmanovic and I spoke, I sensed some concern on his part travelling into the UNTAES region as we call it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you able to be more specific as to what it was that made you sense this concern?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Actually he mentioned that he had a concern, and as we discussed it my suggestion was that in order to facilitate his entry into the region, that we send UN vehicles so that he could easily access the region.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you say -- did you have a discussion with him as to where the UN vehicles might pick him up?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We had indicated that it would be between the two checkpoints, between the UNTAES checkpoint and the checkpoint for Serbia, on the Erdut bridge.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you then proceed to make arrangements in connection with this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did he say to you when you suggested -- did you suggest to him that this was the point where you might pick him up, or was this a suggestion that came from him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At this point, I do not actually recall who suggested it to who, but as we were both having the conversation it resulted in that this would be a good means. It is not atypical that we send the Transitional Administrator's vehicles to pick up different guests as they come into the UNTAES region.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This particular part of the territory at Erdut where this bridge is, do you know where the border lies at that place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know. I simply know that it is an area between the area that is the UNTAES checkpoint and recognises the region and between the checkpoint that is the official checkpoint of the Serbian government.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether or not this border line, if you might call it that, between the two territories, is settled in relation to the parties on either side?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My best understanding is that it is not that -- not necessarily for that specific instance, but for others, when we have looked specifically in the area of Elok which is to the south of the region on various different maps, be they from the United States mapping agency or the United Nations or other maps, there is typically controversy as to where that line was or is. Under the government of Yugoslavia, that, of course, was simply not as important as it was in fact one government.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you happen to know where the border line runs -- sorry, I withdraw that. Do you happen to know where the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia asserts that its border line runs in relation to the bridge at Erdut?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am not sure exactly what their position is, but if you take a look at where they have set their checkpoint up, it is certainly not on the bridge, but it is on a piece of land that is east of the Erdut bridge.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The checkpoint on the Croatian side, if I can call it that, on the Erdut side of the bridge, are you able to say, is that manned by Croatian police or by UNTAES?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At that particular period in time it was monitored by UNTAES military, UNTAES border monitors.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What does that entail, when you say that it was monitored?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Basically that those individuals with the border monitors being the lead organisation responsible for the checkpoint, and I believe TPF was involved as well and that stands for the Transitional Police Force, is required to check identification of vehicles, both entering and leaving the region, as well as performing weapons checks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Apart from the matters that you have already testified to, do you recall whether Mr. Dokmanovic said anything else in relation to this proposed meeting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not at this present time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he agree that he would meet the UN vehicles at the place that you had designated and at the time that you had designated?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he did and the time that was suggested was 3.00, which would allow for ample travel time from that location to the Transitional Administrator's office.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If UNTAES vehicles are to travel into the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, are they permitted to do that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: UNTAES vehicles, yes, are permitted to do that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it necessary for members of the staff of UNTAES to obtain any special form of permission to travel into Federal Republic of Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, they are not. They need to produce their credentials as they go through the checkpoint to the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall having a conversation -- in the course of the conversation with Mr. Dokmanovic, do you recall mentioning the fact that there was a picture apparently that Mr. Klein had of Dokmanovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did. In fact, Mr. Klein had indicated to me that he had a picture and that at some point in the future when he saw Mr. Dokmanovic, that he wanted to give him that picture. I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was your next involvement in the matter, in this matter, after making these arrangements over the telephone?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After I had made those arrangements over the telephone, my next interaction that had to do with anything surrounding this matter was receiving a phone call on Friday evening from Mr. Dokmanovic's son.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you at any stage in the course of the conversation with Mr. Dokmanovic give him an assurance that he would not be arrested if he came into the area of UNTAES?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I had indicated to him that by providing vehicles, we could assure that he would not have a problem entering the UNTAES region.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Apart from telling him that, did you say anything else to him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There is no way that I could provide any guarantees of anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I have no further questions, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: Mr. Fila? Cross-examined by MR. FILA

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Hryshchyshyn, my name is Toma Fila and I am Defence counsel for Mr. Dokmanovic and I would like to ask you several questions. You said two things that for me are contradictory. One is that you were giving no guarantees and the second that you guaranteed to Mr. Dokmanovic that it would be a UN vehicles that would allow him to enter UNTAES territory, if I understood you correctly.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Perhaps you did not understand what I said exactly. Mr. Dokmanovic was concerned about having a problem entering the UNTAES area. In order to assist with that concern, I suggested that we provide vehicles that have the ability to enter our region automatically without checks as a means of ensuring that he enter the region. That is something that is typically done. It is standard policy that any UN vehicle that enters through any of the checkpoints, whether international or internal to Croatia, are permitted free access into the region, so that simply is in consonance with the standards UNTAES policy.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And since when has it become a problem entering the territory of Croatia, all of us entering UNTAES have no problems. Anyone can enter the territory of UNTAES. Obviously they have a problem leaving or trying to leave the UNTAES, but as for entering that territory or better still, who have you given guarantees of safety for entering the UNTAES territory and those persons have not asked for guarantees for leaving the UNTAES territory?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, it is simply not possible for anyone to enter the UNTAES region. They need to have appropriate credentials in order to do that. They need to have forms of identification that are acceptable for entry into the UNTAES area. All the vehicles that are stopped are subject to inspections. Those inspections including inspections for weapons, so that it is simply not a totally permeable border. It is, in fact, a checkpoint not only for entering the region but also for exiting the region. So in both directions, there is a standard protocol that is established.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So anyone who does not have that would be arrested; that is so in all of the world, including UNTAES. What I want to know is: did Mr. Dokmanovic ask any guarantees from you that he would be able to enter and then be arrested by the Croats or anybody else? Why would he need a guarantee? He can enter? You know that he had been the President of the Municipal Assembly. You know that his son is employed by you, by UNTAES. Why would he need any guarantees to enter UNTAES? How do you explain that, without him asking guarantees for leaving UNTAES. Does that seem logical to you, Mr. Hryshchyshyn?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: During the conversation it was my impression that Mr. Dokmanovic had concerns about the checkpoint in either direction, that there were simply concerns about that whole issue.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is okay. Now it is okay, thank you. Not just to enter, because that makes no sense. Second question: you told us that it is common practice for you to send vehicles when Mr. Klein is receiving guests.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Were those vehicles normally used by Mr. Klein, the ones that you sent to pick up Mr. Dokmanovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they were. In fact --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is enough, thank you. Does that mean that Mr. Dokmanovic was Mr. Klein's guest?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: Mr. Fila, you need to allow the witness to respond to the question --

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: I did ask.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: Did you complete your answer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not on the last answer. If I may be permitted. I would like to finish my complaint. One thing I think is important is I think the issue is more simply than entering and leaving the region. During the conversation, I sensed Mr. Dokmanovic was concerned about being seen in the region and that was one of the reasons that those particular vehicles were sent, because him being in those vehicles, having tinted windows, being the vehicles of the Transitional Administrator, that anybody living within the region would not necessarily know who was in that vehicle, so that is I think a very important point. Thank you, your Honour, for permitting me to expand upon that, as to why we had suggested and had those available, so I guess the point I am making is that there is more of a concern than just in and out of the region. The concern was also him being seen within the region. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Thank you, because that is exactly what Mr. Dokmanovic says, exactly what you have just told us. So there is no reason for any discussion between you and I because what Mr. Dokmanovic says is exactly the same. My question is the following: Mr. Hryshchyshyn said it was common practice to send vehicles to the Yugoslav territory when people they need to pick up are Mr. Klein's guests. Was Mr. Dokmanovic a guest of Mr. Klein?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mr. Dokmanovic was proceeding to a mutually agreed upon meeting between UNTAES and himself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question to you was, and you answered Mr. Niemann's question that it was common practice that Mr. Klein sent his vehicle for his own guests to the Yugoslav territory, and that is something we agree upon. Does that mean that Mr. Dokmanovic was a guest of Mr. Klein? He either was or was not. Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It depends on what you classify as a guest.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Excuse me, but those whom you arrest and send to Scheveningen, I do not consider them guests. That I would not include under the term guest.

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: A guest is someone who comes to visit you for lunch, for dinner. A guest is a person you receive at your home. You are Ukranian, I am Yugoslav, I believe we both know what a guest is.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, let me correct the record. I am an American.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A guest is somebody you receive at your home. I am of Greek descent. I am sorry, I did not mean to insult you. I do apologise. Without any hard feelings. What I wanted to say, when somebody visits you at your home, that is a guest. When you invite someone somewhere, that is a guest. If Mr. Dokmanovic was a guest, that does not fit into the ambush that was set up later. He was either a guest or he was not a guest. That is what I understand as the term guest. So let us try it this way --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: Did Mr. Klein invite Mr. Dokmanovic into his home?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, he did not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: Okay. Let us work with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Did Mr. Klein really have a meeting with Mr. Dokmanovic at 3.00? Let us try it this way.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was a meeting that was scheduled. That meeting did not take place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the moment when you were scheduling the meeting, did you know that he was to be arrested as soon as he had crossed the border, because this was a distance of several hundred metres.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I certainly knew that that would be a possibility.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So as far as you are concerned, the other possibility was that he would go to the meeting and he would collect the photograph from Mr. Klein?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Mr. Klein there at the time? Was he waiting for him to give him the photograph at 3.00?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The meeting was scheduled for 3.30. The meeting time in Erdut was scheduled for 3.00.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I do understand that, but was Mr. Klein there and was he waiting for him with the photograph that you said he had had? Was he waiting for Mr. Dokmanovic to appear, or Mr. Klein was not there at all?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mr. Klein had on his schedule the meeting with Mr. Dokmanovic. Mr. Klein that afternoon was on his way back from Zagreb. He was in transit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question was: on that day at 15.30, was Mr. Klein at the place where he was supposed to meet Mr. Dokmanovic, not where he was returning from or where he was going; was he there, same as you are here now?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, he was delayed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So he was not there. When did he arrive? Did he arrive at all? Because as far as I know, he was in Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was in Zagreb, he was returning from a trip, he did return. I do not know exactly what time he returned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So do you still insist that the meeting really was scheduled for Mr. Klein and Mr. Dokmanovic with the possibility of actually attending a meeting, or was that just a trap, a set-up that you needed in order to arrest him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When I had scheduled the meeting with Mr. Dokmanovic, I had checked Mr. Klein's flight arrangements, and when he was to arrive into the region. I had set up that meeting so that Mr. Klein would be there at 3.30 in his office to meet Mr. Dokmanovic. During the course of Friday, there was a late scheduled flight which accounted for why Mr. Klein appeared late, but when we scheduled the meeting, yes, it was such that Mr. Klein would be in his office at 3.30 at UNTAES headquarters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay, so when did you find out that he was to be arrested if he crosses the border, if you found that out at all, I am sorry; if you knew that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I knew that certainly that there was a warrant for Mr. Dokmanovic and I knew that that was a possibility.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who organised the ambush at the UNTAES checkpoint in Erdut if it was not you and you are the military advisor?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I object to the use of the word ambush.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: I will sustain your objection. Who organised the arrest? Do not use the word "ambush". That carries with it certain connotations of illegality and that is an issue for the court to resolve. Do you understand, Mr. Fila? Who made the arrangements for the arrest if not you, rather than ambush.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Okay. Who organised the arrest if it was not you and these were UNTAES soldiers? Could that be done by somebody else without your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it certainly could. Let me help explain. I have a title of military assistant, I do not report to the force commander; nor do any of the military troops report to me, so there is no line of authority within that structure as well. What UNTAES military soldiers do, that is not authorised by me, nor do I necessarily know what all their activities are at any given point in time. That is a matter for the force commander. With regard to your question of who organised it, I am not sure. What I know is that I know that ICTY made the arrest. That I can tell you for certain.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The court is a building where judges are, but somebody had to do it. Who were the people? The court cannot arrest, it is the police or the army that arrests, but not the court. The court can instruct or give orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may, I will object to any questions which are endeavouring to ascertain who the particular military unit were, but that may not have been the question, it may just have been the way I understood the interpretation of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: I will overrule your objection. It is not the unit. I have a question as to whether it was --

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: That was not what I wanted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: -- whether it was UNTAES or the Office of the Prosecutor that made the arrest. You have said that ICTY made the arrest, and what Mr. Fila is saying is that we judges are part of ICTY as well, so certainly you are not saying that we made the arrest.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, it is my understanding, because at that time I was in my office and I only know the situation after it was reported, that there were UNTAES personnel, military personnel involved in the detainment of Mr. Dokmanovic, but that the actual apprehension was made by investigators from the International War Crimes Tribunal. It is my understanding that they served the warrant and made the arrest.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: That is what I asked. Just to clarify the issue on the border; the vehicles which, as you said, belonged to Mr. Klein, which side of your checkpoint were they at? Were they on the Croatian side or the other side?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Those vehicles --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Or let me just ask, do you understand? If this is the checkpoint, this is where Erdut is, this is Bogojevo (indicates). So where were they?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If you take a look at the area, between the two checkpoints is the Erdut bridge. It is my understanding that Mr. Dokmanovic entered UNTAES vehicles in an area between those two checkpoints, so it was not within Serbia, not within the land mass of Croatia, but it was on the bridge.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So then you know for certain exactly where the border is, if you are making such a claim. If you can claim that that was neither the territory of Croatia nor the territory of Serbia, then you are the only person who knows whose territory it is, because there is no such thing as no man's land. It has to be someone's.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My understanding is that there are many borders that remain uncertain. The one thing that we know for sure is that through patrolling, surveillance, a nation exercising their sovereignty over a piece of land, that over that bridge, neither did the Republic of Croatia nor the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia exercise any sovereignty over that area. In other words, had the two checkpoints been located immediately adjacent to each other, I could tell you exactly what was what.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, you just said that that was neither the territory of Croatia nor the territory of Serbia and that is not possible. It has to be somebody's territory. How far do the Yugoslav forces patrol? How far do their patrols reach? Is it to the middle of the bridge? Is there a building, is there a sentry post there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is my understanding that the Serbian militia --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Not militia, army.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That I have never heard any account or seen any account where they come through that checkpoint and on to the bridge. To go back, to expound on your further previous question, I am not an expert in these matters, far from it, but I am also aware of the concept that there are areas in the world that are termed international areas, whether it relates to water or land masses or whatever, and those international areas are used commonly by more than one nation. I think the thing that is most germane here is that the vehicles were positioned on the bridge (i) in order to facilitate the entry and (ii) that the vehicles did not go into the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia to be subject to --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me ask you something else?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To be subject to checks on the border.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: Mr. Fila, let the witness finish, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think I finished the sentence, but let me just finish it. In other words, the region that they were positioned on the bridge there is so that the UNTAES vehicles would not have to go through the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia's checkpoint and then have to turn around and come back through that checkpoint again. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Did you offer Mr. Dokmanovic for the vehicles to be sent to Sombor to pick him up from his home?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not offer that, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You did not. My last question: at that bridge are there UNTAES patrols controlling that area, that particular space, since the Yugoslav police are not controlling it, since Croatian police is not controlling it, so is it UNTAES controlling the area or are they standing behind their checkpoint? Is that the UNTAES area of responsibility, to put it in simple words?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is my understanding that neither side has responsibility for that area, that typically both parties are positioned at their checkpoints, that I am not aware of -- that is me, I am not aware of any routine patrolling back and forth in between those two checkpoints. The Yugoslav, the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia authorities are at their checkpoint and the UNTAES officials are at their checkpoint.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That territory. Finally, according to the UN resolution which places UNTAES in the territory of Eastern Slavonija et cetera, exactly what their authorities are according to the UN resolution and not according to the agreement between you and the Tribunal regarding uncovering and arresting persons suspected of having committed war crimes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Is that a question?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: I think it is. Do you wish to respond to that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do. In the Security Council resolution that establishes UNTAES as a mission, it specifically states that the Transitional Administrator has complete executive authority over the area that is defined as Eastern Slavonija, Baranja and Western Srem. Further in that same resolution, it specifically states that UNTAES is directed to co-operate and assist ICTY as part of its mandate. So if you pull a copy of the Security Council resolution, it clearly states it in that document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: Do you have additional questions, Mr. Fila?

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Yes. And it is related exactly to which territory, this authority of Mr. Klein? Everything you said is correct, but for exactly which territory of UNTAES?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As I mentioned earlier, it is defined as the area of Eastern Slavonija, Baranja and Western Srem. That is known as the UNTAES region.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So outside that territory, you have no authority whatsoever in the territory of Yugoslavia or any other territory that is not within UNTAES.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct. We are specifically mandated with authority within that region.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: Mr. Niemann?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: No, your Honour, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: Mr. Hryshchyshyn, a few questions. Mr. Klein is the Transitional Administrator; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, your Honour, I am sorry, Mr. Klein was the Transitional Administrator during that period of time, yes, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So he was at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he left his functions as of 1st August this year.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If authority was to be given by UNTAES to detain Mr. Dokmanovic, what person would have the authority to give such an order? Would it be Mr. Klein at that time or were there other individuals who could give such an order?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There are other individuals authorised with what I will call the executive authorities of the region. Mr. Klein has a deputy, Mr. Klein also -- had at that point in time, past tense -- had a force commander as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who gave the order to detain Mr. Dokmanovic, if you know? Who within UNTAES?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am not really sure who gave that order.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether any UNTAES official participated with Mr. Curtis, Mr. Kevin Curtis, with the office of the Tribunal Prosecutor, to encourage Mr. Dokmanovic to come to Eastern Slavonija for the purpose of being arrested?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As I understand the situation, your Honour, representatives of ICTY had ongoing conversations with Mr. Dokmanovic, reference war crimes sites, that was their primary business, as I understand it, with him. As they were having conversations, it was my understanding that there were various physical locations within the region that he wanted to point out to them very specifically. As it has been related to me, during the course of those conversations and during discussions when Mr. Klein's name was mentioned, that indicated that he did not see Mr. Klein for a long time, and was interested in visiting the region.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you spoke with Mr. Dokmanovic on, what was that, 26th, was it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, that would have been the 25th, a Wednesday.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that the first time that you spoke with him concerning a meeting with Mr. Klein?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During this time period at least.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At that point in time, did you know that arrangements were in effect for UNTAES personnel to detain Mr. Dokmanovic when he came to Eastern Slavonija on June 27th?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I knew at that point that there was a warrant that had been issued.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You testified to that. You are the deputy, or were the -- you are the military assistant to the Transitional Administrator.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What I am asking you is, when you were talking with Mr. Dokmanovic on the 25th, two days later he comes to the region and is detained by UNTAES, you say arrested by the Office of the Prosecutor. Did you know when you were talking to him that plans were in place to detain him should he come in the next couple of days to the area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I certainly knew that was a possibility.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that a possibility because a warrant was out for his arrest or a possibility because plans were being made for that purpose?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I knew it was a possibility because there was a warrant for his arrest.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: With regards to plans --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is the first time that this happened in this area, is that not so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am asking you, did you know at this time that plans were in place to detain Mr. Dokmanovic if he came in the next two days?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were plans that if a war criminal were to enter Eastern Slavonija --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I realise that and I realise there was a warrant for his arrest. You are the military assistant to the Transitional Administrator. It seems to me if plans were in place to detain him, you would have known about it two days before he comes. Maybe I am wrong.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I am just trying to remember the incident clearly, because I want to make sure I give the court --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It is the first time it happened. I thought it ought to stick in your mind. It was not that long ago.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At that point in time I knew that there would be a likelihood or a possibility of him being detained.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You spoke with him about setting up a meeting with Mr. Klein to discuss property matters of Serbs.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It is your testimony that Mr. Klein intended on going through with that meeting, is that not so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct; in other words when we scheduled it, it was our intent that Mr. Klein would be in Vukovar and be available for that meeting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you first hear about the possibility of Mr. Dokmanovic coming to Eastern Slavonija to talk with Mr. Klein about property matters?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On 24th June.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who told you about that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Representatives from the Tribunal that were working in Eastern Slavonija.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they tell you that should he come, they wanted UNTAES to detain him for the purposes of being arrested?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They indicated that if he did come they requested our assistance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you at that time promise that you would give that assistance?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I indicated that we would co-operate with them as we were mandated.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You referred to the resolution, the resolution that is the resolution dated January 15th 1996, it states in paragraph 10, there is a military component and a civilian component. I have read through that. Can you point out what subsection of 10 or 11 authorises UNTAES to detain indictees of the Tribunal? I have a marked up copy, but I do not mind sharing it with you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That would be useful. (Handed).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you see paragraph 10 and paragraph 11? It is on the third page, I think.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I do not see anything specifically there, but if you turn to paragraph 22, I think it is --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 21, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The Security Council repeats its --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In fact, paragraph 21 goes on to say: "Stresses that UNTAES shall co-operate with the International Tribunal in the performance of its mandate, including with regard to the protection of the sites identified by the Prosecutor and persons conducting investigations of the International Tribunal."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And paragraph 20 reaffirms that all states shall co-operate fully with the International Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia and its organs in accordance with the provisions of resolution 827, 1993, of 25th May 1993, and the statute of the International Tribunal and shall comply with requests for assistance or orders issued by the Trial Chamber under Article 29 of the statute. Do you know what Article 29 of the statute provides? I am sure you have not memorised it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Unfortunately not off the top of my head.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Article 29 says, let us see: "Co-operation and judicial assistance." It says in (ii): "States shall comply without undue delay with any request for assistance or an order issued by a Trial Chamber, including but not limited to", and then subsection (d) says: "The arrest or detention of persons." So Article 29 specifically mentions that States have a duty to arrest or detain persons, but it is your position that UNTAES has that responsibility as well because of the obligation to co-operate under paragraph 21 of this resolution; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct. As I best understand it, from a layman's point of view, the Republic of Croatia does not exert sovereignty over the area known as Eastern Slavonija, Baranja and Western Srem but typically the sovereignty that would be exercised by a nation for that particular land mass that I just described, is the responsibility of the United Nations and in particular UNTAES, so my understanding would be that UNTAES would be functioning as a state, or the executive authority, or the organisation that has sovereignty and is responsible until it is fully reintegrated into the Republic of Croatia, so that it would have the same obligations as a State would in performance of its duties and responsibilities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that UNTAES would have authority to arrest an indictee of the Tribunal in Eastern Slavonija; is that not so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That would be my understanding. Further that the police force in that region, which is called the Transitional Police Force or the TPF, is specifically responsible to the Transitional Administrator and not to the Republic of Croatia, so that in the administration of the -- what I will call policing functions, that that is UNTAES's responsibility.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether UNTAES has received any complaint from Croatia regarding the detention and subsequent arrest by the Prosecution's office of Mr. Dokmanovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To the best of my knowledge I do not have any knowledge of a complaint that has been received by UNTAES from the Republic of Croatia relative to this case.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The basic agreement that is referred to in that resolution; is that an agreement then between Croatia and the Serbian community? Are you familiar at all with that basic agreement, and if so, does it contain any matters that perhaps relate to the detention and arrest of Mr. Dokmanovic? We have not been provided with a copy of it. That is why I am asking you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am familiar with that agreement, your Honour. It is the basic agreement, some time referred to as the (inaudible) agreement. It was signed on 12th November 1995. It called for a period of up to two years, actually specifically written as one year, and if either party decided or requested that it be extended, that could have a full term of two years. It was an agreement between the government of Croatia and the local Serbian community in Eastern Slavonija, Baranja and Western Srem and an agreement that was witnessed by ambassador Peter Galbraith of the United Nations and special representative Thorwald Stoltenberg from the United Nations. It was an agreement signed to prevent further military conflict and lead towards more peaceful process of reintegration of that area back into the Republic of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: Maybe we will take a look at it and make a determination for ourselves. Are there additional questions, Mr. Niemann?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: Mr. Fila? Further cross-examined by MR. FILA

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would just like to clarify one point. Did the Minister of Foreign Affairs of Yugoslavia protest against the arrest of Mr. Dokmanovic? Is it the position of Yugoslavia that you have violated its sovereignty? I am referring to Mr. Milutinovic. I have his letter.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am familiar with Minister Milutinovic, as we have met many times. We did receive a letter from Mr. Milutinovic in protest.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What does it say?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not recall the full text of his letter/fax to Transitional Administrator Klein, but it was a letter of protest. I must, however, go on to say that in a subsequent meeting with the most senior authorities of the Serbian government that this matter was specifically discussed between transitional Administrator Klein and senior Serbian government officials, and in that meeting, after a discussion, there was no continued protest or hard feelings or a continued adverse situation that was created as a result of this apprehension and arrest.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Excuse me, has this protest been withdrawn? What was the reason why there was no bad blood? Did Mr. Milutinovic withdraw the protest, if that is how things stand? I know for a fact that he did not. The Minister of Foreign Affairs of Yugoslavia, that is Mr. Milutinovic and it is an independent and sovereign State. So, has this protest been withdrawn?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In an official sense, via correspondence or a follow on letter, I have no knowledge of that. However, I need to point to a meeting between President Milosevic, Foreign Minister Milutinovic and Transitional Minister Klein when the matter was discussed, and upon conclusion of that meeting there were no indications of a continued protest or any further action by the Serbian government.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: Mr. Fila, if this relates -- do you have additional questions? I wanted to refer to Exhibit 11.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: I am finishing. What was the response among the population after the arrest of Mr. Dokmanovic in the territory controlled by UNTAES? Was there any harassment? Did you receive protests from any organisations and did the people start to move out more rapidly and is this the reason why you had discussions with Mr. Milosevic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Let me start with your last question, I will work backwards. No, that specifically was not the reason we had the meeting with President Milosevic. This particular case was one of a whole list of issues. The Transitional Administrator meets with both the President of Croatia and the President, at that point in time, of Serbia on a routine basis to discuss issues, since this is a region that involves ethnic groups, both ethnic groups, and is also on a border situation. It was not a specific meeting to talk about this case. As it relates to the reaction by the local residents within the region, initially there was a concern that was voiced by the citizens. Yes, I believe we did receive at least one letter of protest and that may have been from Dr Stanimirovic, one of the local leaders, or Mr. Vujinovic, I do not recall exactly who drafted it, but there was some concern --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Stanimirovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It could very well be. I do not recall at this specific time. The key point though was that there was some what I would call mild reaction, the duration was very short, for a couple of days, and it is difficult to tell whether the reaction was specific to the individual or more to the apprehension of suspected war criminals in general. However, I will be quite frank with you, any adverse reaction, which again I will classify as mild, dissipated very quickly. In fact the reaction throughout the population was what I will call mixed, in that there were both people who were concerned and people who were -- who realised that it was the international community's responsibility to exercise indictments that were issued from this court, so that there was not a consensus on the region as a whole with regard to the reaction of this specific incident. Additionally, it was reported subsequent to this arrest that individuals -- certain individuals were further concerned who may or may not have participated in some kind of illegal activities, exited the region after this particular case, so the reaction was mixed, and at best, it was mild and quickly dissipated.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My last question: since we know to speed things up that there is a police force that is under UNTAES's control, it is a mixed Serbian and Croatian police force; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can this police force effect arrests or do you have to call the UNTAES soldiers to effect arrests?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, the police can arrest people.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: Mr. Niemann?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: When we return from recess we will hear from the Registrar. I wanted her to clarify some matters regarding the warrant for arrest. Then we will hear closing submissions from the parties and we would like to finish by 5.30, if we can. Everyone would like us to finish by 5.30 but we cannot continue into tomorrow because there is one courtroom and there are two trials going on. Relating to Defence Exhibit 11, Mr. Williamson, you had objected to Defence Exhibit 11 before which was -- was that the protest from the Foreign Minister of Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I do not believe either one of those came from Yugoslavia. One of them was a letter from Mr. Stanimirovic, who is the leader of the local Serbs in Eastern Slavonija, and one was from a non-governmental organisation. It is my understanding that Mr. Fila had previously submitted the letter from Mr. Milutinovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: Thank you. We will stand until recess until 4.45. You are permanently excused. Thank you. (The witness withdrew) (4.30 pm) (A short break) (4.45 pm)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: I have asked the Registrar to be present at this hearing at this point in time to explain the circumstances surrounding what is in evidence as Defence Exhibit 13, that is the warrant for arrest, one version is in Serbo-Croatian, the other is in English. Mrs. De Sampaya? Are we not operating? Is there nothing on the monitors? We took a rather short break in the interests of trying to finish up at 5.30. (Pause). As I indicated, I have asked the Registrar to be present at the hearing to speak to Defence Exhibit 13 which is the warrant for arrest for Mr. Dokmanovic. There is a copy in Serbo-Croatian and a copy in English that is a part of Defence Exhibit 13. Mrs. De Sampaya? MRS. DE SAMPAYA: Thank you. As I have understood the question to be is what is the status of the Exhibit 13. There is an original warrant of arrest signed on 3rd April 1996 by Judge Riad that was not disclosed and that was sent later, in July 1996, to UNTAES. My view is that the original document, the original order by the judge, which was signed by him, is a version, it is a warrant of arrest in the English language. A copy had been attached in Serbo-Croatian. As you may appreciate, at the Registry, we are not able to read and to verify whether the exact wording of the translation is correct. It now appears that that translation in Serbo-Croatian was based upon an error, although it carries the name of the addressee correctly, as it has been addressed to UNTAES it was further the version which was to be directed to the Croatian government -- I mean the translation, that is, but I understand, too, that has been corrected. It is a mistake, without any doubt, and as we all know we try to reduce the number of mistakes that we human beings make, but it is simply a translation and it is not an original document that was in any way wrong. The original document as signed by Judge Riad on 3rd April, and later forwarded, is the correct version, but that is in the English language. Thank you. (Pause).

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: As I understand it, Mrs. De Sampaya, then subsequently when it was learned that the Serbo-Croatian version of the English warrant that was signed by Judge Riad on April 3rd 1996, when it was discovered that that Serbo-Croatian copy only indicated that it was to be sent to the Republic of Croatia, that that was subsequently amended and the one in Serbo-Croatian that is now a part of the Registry files indicates that it is to be sent to both UNTAES and to the Republic of Croatia; is that correct? MRS. DE SAMPAYA: It was not sent to Croatia because it was an order by the judge telling us that there was no need to disclose it to and send it to the Republic of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: Okay. It need not be made a record in these proceedings if it is in the files of the Registry, and, of course, the Defence and the Prosecution will have an opportunity to obtain a copy at this time, because it is not under seal any longer; is that correct? MRS. DE SAMPAYA: I understand that copies have been sent to the parties, to the parties here present.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: The corrected one? MRS. DE SAMPAYA: The corrected version, yes. Mr. Fila, are you saying that you have received a copy of the corrected Serbo-Croatian warrant of arrest, the one that should correspond to the one signed by Judge Riad on April 3rd 1996 in English?

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Your Honour, there was an objection that at the moment of arrest Mr. Dokmanovic received a warrant of arrest which clearly said that he should be arrested about the State of Croatia. I do not care about the corrections made later. At the moment of arrest Mr. Dokmanovic is supposed to receive a correct version. Since I have not been arrested by anybody yet, I do not need to receive the amended version. We are emphasising this to you for a simple reason, that in this document on three different occasions the word UNTAES was translated with Croatia. It is impossible to make such an error and it is not a minor error, white or green or another colour. UNTAES cannot be translated as the Republic of Croatia. That is why we are indicating this, because this was a deliberate error. They did not know that there was a Mr. Knezevic who would see this, because he was a Serb -- to believe he was arrested by the state of Croatia. He received it in Serbo-Croatian because he does not speak English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: Do you mean Mr. Dokmanovic who would receive this? Okay, fine. Mr. Niemann, do you have any comment regarding this matter?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: Very good. Thank you very much for coming, Mrs. De Sampaya. If there are no questions, then let us continue with closing remarks. Mr. Fila?

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Your Honour, respecting the time as agreed upon, I intend to be very brief, because everything that we had to say had already been submitted in writing and we have, both the Prosecution and ourselves, we have all changed our opinion several times. The first objection was the territory where the arrest was carried out, because that territory is not the territory controlled by UNTAES, and that, I believe, is undeniable, that both Dokmanovic and Knezevic, not the jury but defector, were deprived of their freedom outside the checkpoint of UNTAES forces. Second, that UNTAES organised an ambush that was also never disputed. Also third, from Mr. Curtis's testimony, it was obvious that he went to see him to lure him for, we claim that according to the UN resolution, UNTAES does not have such authority. Fifth , that Rule 59 of this honourable court, the Tribunal, cannot overpower a UN resolution. Sixth, that examples given such as Adolf Eichman, Klaus Barbie and others represent the behaviour of a particular state. The security council reacted to such behaviours of different states, finding that the sovereignty of Argentina was threatened and the Israeli terrorist forces attack at the Entebe airport resulted in a convention of terrorism which banned such actions for the future. Then this honourable Tribunal does not represent the court of a State, it represents courts of all the States. It is binding even for the States that are not UN members, so this is a court of all courts, and it has to act in such a way that all the UN member States are respected by the statute of your court. Your Honour sanctions are foreseen as well as consequences for those not honouring requests of the court. In Eichman's case, Israel could not apply Argentina's sanctions, but the security council could apply sanctions against my country and they have done it for a few years. I am not talking about individual actions of the United States, but we did have UN sanctions, security council sanctions. Therefore, there is a question of lack of co-operation of Yugoslavia with this Tribunal. We have submitted to you a citation of the Yugoslav constitution and that is disputed between the authorities of Yugoslavia and the Tribunal, if the co-operation with this Tribunal includes extradition, which is the term we use, of citizens of Yugoslavia, but only citizens of Yugoslavia. There was never any problem in our State in extraditing persons who are not citizens of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia at the request of the Tribunal; for example, Erdemovic was not kidnapped by UNTAES or through one Curtis, but he was sent at the request of the Tribunal and brought here. Erdemovic was born and lived in the same republic as Mr. Dokmanovic. If Yugoslavia had refused to extradite Mr. Dokmanovic, they would have risked sanctions. Therefore, there is no basis in the claim of the Prosecution that Yugoslavia is not co-operating when it comes to individuals who are not citizens of Yugoslavia. Such an operation, in addition to being very damaging in its consequences in people leaving the area, I will just say that if criminals are running away, that is damaging, but there have been mistaken identifications at this court. I will remind Mr. Niemann of Goran Lajic, who had spent almost three months here and it was determined that that was not the person. Then persons who are guilty and persons who are not guilty are both fleeing. This was a badly executed operation, an operation that does not contribute to the reputation of this court or the UN or anybody else. That is the reason why we are reacting in this way. Confidence is threatened, safety of people is threatened. I have said and Mr. Williamson has answered, I hope that nobody would have any reactions against these children from UNTAES because they really have done nothing they can be guilty of, but what is dangerous is what could happen tomorrow when another Curtis wants to talk to somebody else. Sovereignty of Yugoslavia has been violated. The UN symbol has been abused because UN vehicles were used to lure, if nothing else, Mr. Dokmanovic and he was later kidnapped. A trap was organised in Erdut. You have heard statements of three witnesses. There are many differences in their statements. Mr. Interpreter, whose name we are not using, said that Mr. Hryshcyhshyn offered to send vehicles to Sombor where Dokmanovic lived. Curtis confirmed this, but Hryshcyhshyn said no, so it is obvious that Mr. Dokmanovic was not a guest of Mr. Klein's, but rather that there was an organised effort to bring him there so that he could be legitimately arrested. Nobody can convince me that from April 3rd 1996, His Honour Judge Riad, on the back page of the arrest warrant, he did say where he was, where Mr. Dokmanovic was. A fax transmission was enough for the police to arrest him, because if you were listening to Mr. Hryshchyshyn, it would seem that there is nobody else in the territory of Slavonija except for UNTAES. There are very strong police forces directly commanded by Mr. Klein and they could have arrested him in the municipality with no problems. What was the reason for this delay from April 3rd until June? Was there an important arrival of somebody from the US administration or something else, I do not know. But the fact that this was done very badly, that my country's integrity was violated, that the reaction of even the Croatian Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Madam Hodak, the assistant, her view was that they could not do it this way, to stroll around Croatia and Serbia any way they wanted. I do not think there is any State in the world that would allow people to roam around and arrest people without the State knowing. I have filed several verdicts. I understood the cases of Barbie and Eichman, but that is one State who sent its forces to another State and did what they did and the UN did condemn it. In this case, with everything I have already written, I do believe that if you appreciate this type of arrest, I think this will be very damaging and confusing. There is no problem for him to return to Yugoslavia and for you to instruct the Yugoslav court to send him back immediately. Then there would be a legitimate decision, and there could be no prevention for this because he is not a citizen of Yugoslavia, he is a refugee with a fully recognised refugee status. That is not the same as the status of a citizen. I believe there is no need for me to explain this to you. From the documents I submitted it is clearly visible where he was born and which citizenship he has before the war. During the Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, we had double citizenship of the Republic; for example I was a citizen of Macedonia. I am of Greek descent, I was a Macedonian citizen, I requested, I guess two years ago, citizenship of Yugoslavia and now I am protected, according to our judicial theory. I do not need to go into that, Mr. Cassese would not perhaps agree, but that does not matter. In any case, I believe this decision is very important and it is important such actions are not repeated, because I am afraid that concerns for all of us, for those young men doing their jobs would be justified. Thank you very much. I have tried to be brief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: Where was Mr. Dokmanovic born? You indicated it is in the documents you have submitted, I am not sure which exhibit. You can tell me.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Yes. In his identity card, and his passport, both have been submitted. It is the carte d'identite in French, it says from Vukovar. All the documents are from Vukovar. He would not be able to be the head of the Municipal Assembly unless he was from Vukovar. There was no need to do this and I believe this should be said publicly. No need whatsoever. The tape I requested, I did not request it to threaten the lives of those children, of course not, but do believe me that the mistake has been made and it is a grievous mistake. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: Mr. Fila, what are the legal consequences of the delay? The arrest warrant was signed by Judge Riad in April 1996. According to the employment papers of Mr. Dokmanovic's residence was in Sombor as of July something in 1996. What are the legal consequences of the delay?

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: I will explain --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: I understand factually they could have arrested earlier, but what legal rights have been violated because of the delay as opposed to the method of arrest?

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Regarding the fact that he enjoys the status of a refugee in Yugoslavia, any person residing in the territory of Yugoslavia has a certain status, is under protection and control of that State. He was not residing in Yugoslavia illegally. Even then people cannot be arrested there. He had a recognised refugee status, because in 1997 there was a list that appeared of 150 names that contained both his name and Mr. Knezevic's. His wife crossed over in July, crossed over to Sombor, and Dokmanovic had to work for another six months, because that was what he was obliged to do. That is why his contract finished in October. He had a traffic accident. UNTAES conducted an on site investigation because there was nobody else. He could have been arrested by anyone at any time. He had a photograph taken with Mr. Klein. He took part in the negotiations. I see no need for international incidents, and all this row, and so many people leaving Baranja for this. The reason for Milosevic, Milutinovic and Klein's meeting was exactly to calm the situation down. Maybe this could be off the record. People have invested incredible efforts to keep the people there, to prevent them from fleeing, myself personally and Mr. Vujin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: What legal rights have been violated by this delay in the arrest? That is my question. I understand you are saying there was no need to wait that long. I do not know that it has been established that there was not a need. I do not know whether the evidence would show nothing as I can recall as to what was the situation in April 1996, who was available to execute arrest warrants or whatever. Rather than talk about what happened --

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Well UNTAES says --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: Is he entitled to be arrested within 30 days from the execution of the arrest warrant or within a certain period of time, is that what you are saying?

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: No, I want to say that through a UN procedure through the statute, there is a foreseen procedure of arrests. He was a refugee in the territory of an independent state called Yugoslavia. Arrests cannot be carried out on its territory. A request should have been made to Yugoslavia to carry out an arrest. His right was violated because he was arrested in an inhumane way. I am explaining that this would not have happened if this was done properly, if ordinary police had come, because UNTAES does have police, if they had come to arrest him and we would be confirming today or tomorrow whether he was guilty or not. I believe that an illegal arrest was a violation of the sovereignty of Yugoslavia, he was arrested in a very tricky way, and that is simply not acceptable. That is why I made all these submissions, and that is why I believe the UN foresaw all the ways in which an arrest can be carried out. Our Security Council resolution says exactly what UNTAES can do. It does not say that UNTAES can arrest, organise ambushes, et cetera, especially not military ones. Finally, my claim is that the rules of this court cannot carry more power than UN resolutions. Everything that happened actually resulted in an illegal arrest. That is the difference I am trying to indicate. Until October, he was available, even until February or March.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: So it is not your position that an accused is entitled to be arrested within a certain period of time, it is your position that Article 29 of the statute prescribes the sole method for arresting an accused and that is to seek the co-operation of a state and that UNTAES lacks the authority as well as the method for arresting --

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: UNTAES is not a state, and third, and you also have the fact that this warrant of arrest has to be carried out without a delay, that the State is requested to carry it out without undue delay and not when somebody finds it necessary to carry it out in a year, two or three. That is so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: So are you saying then the fact then of a sealed indictment prevents a State from complying with its obligation under Article 29, because it says "executed without undue delay". Does that mean undue delay from the time it receives it or undue delay from the time it is signed by the judge?

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: Which one?

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: It cannot be submitted to them because they do not know, but if a judge issues a warrant of arrest it has to be served to the State where the indictee is. I do not think that indictments are hidden from States, they are hidden from criminals. That is how I understand it. I have not understood Rule 59 as hiding from the State, because States are obliged and they have to carry it out. Otherwise it would have a different meaning, that would mean that we would have parachute forces and we would be carrying out different assaults in different States to pull someone out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Niemann, Mr. Williamson?

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: Your Honours, there has been a substantial amount of written material which has already been submitted on this matter, so I will rely to a large extent on what you already have before you, but I would, however, like to address some of the issues that were raised by Mr. Fila in his argument. In response to his contention that the arrest occurred on the territory of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, he said in his written submissions that the arrest occurred de facto on the territory of the FRY because Mr. Dokmanovic had entered the vehicle on that side of the river. I think from the testimony you have heard today there is some ambiguity as to where the border is located. Clearly all of the testimony indicates that the vehicles were located between the border post on the FRY side and the border post on the Croatian side. At that point in time Mr. Dokmanovic and Mr. Knezevic got into the vehicle voluntarily. According to Mr. Dokmanovic's testimony, up until the point that he was actually removed from the vehicle, he still believed he was going to a meeting with Mr. Klein. There was nothing that occurred during the course of this trip from the Bogojevo side of the river to the Erdut compound which alerted Mr. Dokmanovic to the fact that he was already under arrest. In fact the arrest did occur on Croatian territory, it occurred at Erdut, a kilometre and a half from the bridge. In relation to his argument that UNTAES does not have the authority to make arrests and that it is not in its mandate, I have two points on this. First of all, UNTAES was in possession of a valid warrant of arrest, signed by a judge of this Tribunal. The warrant was issued pursuant to Article 59 bis -- sorry, Rule 59 bis which was a rule promulgated by the judges of the Tribunal; they had in their possession, they therefore had an order of this court to act. It is our contention that they would have been in contravention of a court order had they failed to act. Furthermore, if you read paragraph 21 of the mandate, it states: "Stresses that UNTAES shall co-operate with the International Tribunal in the performance of its mandate, including with regard to the protection of sites identified by the Prosecutor and persons conducting investigations for the International Tribunal." When the UNTAES mandate was enacted by the Security Council in resolution 1037, the issue of arrest was discussed in the United Nations. The representative for Honduras, Mr. Martinez Blanco, stated: "My delegation is of the strong view that any individual who has committed crimes against humanity must be brought to justice. We note that UNTAES will be the sole governing authority in Eastern Slavonija. During the transitional period, and that in accordance with the provisions of this draft resolution and the statute of the International Tribunal, it therefore has the authority to deal with war crimes committed in the former Yugoslavia." Additionally the representative for Egypt, Mr. El-Arabi, stated: "With respect to paragraph 21 of the draft resolution, co-operation between UNTAES and the International Tribunal for the Former Yugoslavia should be comprehensive, with a view to arresting those indicted by the Tribunal and handing them over for trial." No other state contested this interpretation of the UNTAES mandate and it was enacted accordingly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: You realise, Mr. Williamson, that the representative from UNTAES, the military assistant to the Transitional Administrator, has testified that UNTAES did not arrest Mr. Dokmanovic, that the office of the Tribunal Prosecutor arrested him. Do you take a different position?

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: I would say it was a joint operation. You have all seen the videotape and I think it speaks for itself --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: No, it does not.

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: He was placed in physical custody by soldiers of UNTAES.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: When was Mr. Dokmanovic detained, first detained?

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: At the Erdut compound.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: Who detained him?

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: UNTAES military personnel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: Was he arrested at that point? Was he under arrest at that point?

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: I would consider that he was under arrest, yes. He certainly was not free to leave.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: He was not read his rights.

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: He was read his rights immediately thereafter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: He was read his rights when he got to the Erdut base.

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: That is where I am saying was the point he was detained, at the Erdut base.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: When he got in the UN vehicle, that was when he was detained; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: No, I would disagree with that. I am saying that he was detained at the point that he was removed from the UN vehicle at the Erdut compound.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: Before then then he would have been free to get out of the vehicle and leave?

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: I cannot say that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: You have to say that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: I think that is speculation on my part, your Honour, as to how the soldiers in that vehicle would have reacted at that point. The issue I do not think arose. The belief was that if Mr. Dokmanovic entered this vehicle voluntarily, that there was going to be no reason for him to try to leave and, in fact, he did not try to leave, so it is speculation for me to say that the soldiers who were driving the vehicle would have locked the doors and in some way physically detained him within the vehicle had he wished to get out on the Yugoslav side of the bridge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: Mr. Fila, please do not talk while Mr. Williamson is submitting his closing remarks. Mr. Dokmanovic was detained at some point.

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: Our position is that Mr. Dokmanovic was detained when he was removed from the vehicle.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: When was he arrested?

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: At that same moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: Okay. Who arrested him?

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: He was arrested by military personnel from UNTAES and by representatives of the Office of the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: What authority does the Prosecutor's office have to arrest indictees?

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: Under Rule 59 bis --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: That is a rule. What authority in the statute? Article 15.1, I think it is, says that the Prosecutor shall -- let us see. 16.1 details the authorities in the statute now of the Prosecutor. It says: "The Prosecutor shall be responsible for the investigation and Prosecution of persons responsible for serious violations of international humanitarian law committed in the territory of the former Yugoslavia since 1991." There is nothing else in Article 16 that speaks to anything near arrest, detention et cetera, it just says: "The Prosecutor shall be independent, the Office of the Prosecutor shall be composed of", et cetera, et cetera. So 16.1 gives the Prosecutor general responsibility for the investigation and prosecution of persons. Rule 59 bis does provide that the arrest warrant shall be provided to authorities and to the Prosecutor who, upon being taken into custody, shall be transferred.

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: It says: "Order for his transfer to the Tribunal in the event that he be taken into custody by that authority or an international body or the Prosecutor."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: Taken into custody is the same as arrest?

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: That would be my contention.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: So it is 59 bis that gives the Prosecutor the authority to arrest?

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: But you realise that rules, as Mr. Fila argued, cannot go beyond the powers vested in the Prosecutor or, indeed, go beyond the statute in any way. Where in the statute does the Prosecutor have this authority?

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, Article 15 of the statute provides for the adoption of Rules of Procedure and Evidence by the judges for the conduct of the pre-trial phase of the proceedings; trials and appeals; the admission of evidence; the protection of victims and witnesses; and other appropriate matters. Apparently the judges of the Tribunal en banque decided that this was an appropriate rule to be enacted and was necessary for the functioning of the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: Do not throw it back to the judges, with all due respect. Article 29 talks about arrests and that speaks of States co-operating, States complying with orders including the arrest. Can you tell me where is the authority in the statute?

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I am not aware of any specific provision in the statute which authorises the Prosecutor or anyone other than States to make arrests. However, I think the rules have a presumption of validity and it is within the implied powers of the Tribunal to enact rules that are in accordance with the statute.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: Article 20.2 says: "A person against whom an indictment has been confirmed shall, pursuant to an order or an arrest of the International Tribunal, be taken into custody, immediately informed of the charges against him and transferred to the International Tribunal".

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: I am sorry, Article 22?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: Article 20.2. Article 20.2 does not say a State. Article 29 says a State. Article 16.1 speaks generally of the Prosecutor's authorities. Find me somewhere in the statute that will give the Prosecutor authority. If you do not feel there is any authority except in the rules, stand by that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: My position is that the rules have been enacted pursuant to the statute and that the rules allow for the Prosecutor to make arrests, that this is within the implied powers of the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: You realise that rules that do not have a sufficient basis in the statute can be considered invalid? Judges make the rules, but judges make mistakes, do we not? I say I do at least, so I am asking you, if you are looking for authority just in a rule, I think it might be best for you to ground it in the statute, because that is what judges do when we pass the rules. I would suggest that perhaps you look at Article 20.2 or 16.1.

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
